s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial asymmetry with skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement
salient_findings: Progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement of the right side of the nose and cheek
Slightly hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles
key_facts: 10-year history of progressive symptoms
Multiple nondiagnostic skin biopsies
Septorhinoplasty 6 months prior due to collapse of the right nasal ala
Significant submucosal tissue was noted and removed from the right nasal cavity during surgery
Initial improvement after surgery, followed by enlargement of soft tissue and thickening of the overlying skin
Clinical examination revealed hyperplastic soft tissue and dilated patulous follicles
Surgical pathology showed fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation
Skin biopsy was interpreted as sebaceous hyperplasia
Surgical specimens revealed subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density
Thickened and fragmented collagen bundles were observed
Mature adipocytes extended into skeletal tissue

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density and mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue

shortlist.label: Madelung disease
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement of the face

shortlist.label: Lipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple lipomas and subcutaneous tissue involvement

shortlist.label: Fibrous hamartoma of infancy
shortlist.why_kept: Fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation in surgical pathology

shortlist.label: Nuchal-type fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells and thickened collagen bundles

raw.rationale: The presence of subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density, thickened and fragmented collagen bundles, and mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue supports this diagnosis, which is characterized by a mix of fibrous and adipocytic elements.

rejected.label: Madelung disease
rejected.why: Typically involves multiple symmetric lipomatosis, which does not match the unilateral presentation in this case

rejected.label: Lipomatosis
rejected.why: Does not account for the fibrous component and spindle cell proliferation seen in the surgical specimens

rejected.label: Fibrous hamartoma of infancy
rejected.why: The patient's age and the presence of significant adipocytic components do not align with this diagnosis, which is typically seen in infancy

rejected.label: Nuchal-type fibroma
rejected.why: Characterized by a distinct nuchal location and lack of significant adipocytic components, which does not fit the clinical and pathological findings in this case
